basis: Chapter 12 'Feedstuffs': Tab. 12.2 for the production-process shares, Tab. 12.3 (Maize row) for the transport distances and section 12.2.3 for the processing energy (35 kWh electricity and 4 m3 natural gas per tonne of feedstuff). Per 1 kg of feedstuff at the feed mill.

items.name: grain maize IP, at farm
items.per: per kg grain maize IP, at feed mill
items.note: Tab. 12.2: grain maize IP is 10 % import and 90 % CH production, and of the CH production 100 % is IP; the 'values used in ecoinvent data' column is IP 100 / extensive 0 / organic 0. Imports are explicitly approximated by Swiss IP production ('Production abroad is therefore approximated by integrated production ... with location in Switzerland'), so the whole kilogram is drawn from the IP-at-farm module. The table gives shares, not an amount, so 1 kg per kg is the implied value with no processing loss stated.

items.name: electricity, low voltage, at grid
items.quote: electricity and 4 m3 natural gas per tonne of feedstuff. The natural gas was converted into final energy
items.per: per kg grain maize IP, at feed mill
items.note: 'For ecoinvent the values from InfoMil (1996) were used, namely an average of 35 kWh electricity and 4 m3 natural gas per tonne of feedstuff.' - the milling, dosing, mixing and pelleting step.

items.name: natural gas, burned in industrial furnace
items.quote: electricity and 4 m3 natural gas per tonne of feedstuff. The natural gas was converted into final energy
items.per: per kg grain maize IP, at feed mill
items.factor_source: 4 m3/t x 36 MJ/m3 (LHV of natural gas) / 1000 kg/t = 0.144 MJ/kg
items.search: natural gas burned in industrial furnace
items.note: Same sentence: 4 m3 natural gas per tonne. The sentence that says how the gas was converted into final energy is cut off at the page break, so a standard lower heating value of 36 MJ/m3 is used: 4 m3/t x 36 MJ/m3 / 1000 kg = 0.144 MJ/kg.

items.name: transport, lorry 28t
items.per: per kg grain maize IP, at feed mill
items.note: Tab. 12.3, Maize row: 90 km by lorry in Switzerland. 1 kg over 90 km = 0.001 t x 90 km.

items.name: transport, lorry 28t, RER
items.per: per kg grain maize IP, at feed mill
items.note: Tab. 12.3, Maize row: 100 km by lorry in Europe for the 10 % imported share. Barge and overseas ship are 0 for maize.

gaps: The report prints no single unit-process table for 'grain maize IP, at feed mill'; the dataset has to be assembled from three separate tables plus a text sentence, so all amounts are derived rather than read off.
The drying of the maize is documented in chapter 13 (Tab. 13.3, energy per kg of evaporated water) and chapter 14, outside this excerpt, so no drying input is included.
No feed-mill infrastructure and no water use (the flour-mill figures of Salzgeber and Lörcher are explicitly NOT the ones used).
Packaging is explicitly excluded: 'The packaging materials are not considered in the inventories.'
Transport from the feed mill to the regional storehouse or user is explicitly excluded because the inventories refer to 'at feed mill'.
The sentence stating how the 4 m3 of natural gas was converted into final energy is cut off by the page break, so the MJ value rests on a standard heating value.
